Projects, configuration and raw data

Source: vignettes/projects.Rmd
projects.Rmd

Every rendehR function works inside a project: a folder with a configuration file, credentials, and room for the raw and cohort files. This article shows what a project contains, which settings matter, and how several studies can share one copy of the raw data.

The project folder

ehr_init_project() creates the folder and its two configuration files. Nothing is overwritten if they already exist.

library(rendehR)
ehr_init_project(src_name = "mimic_iv_demo", base_dir = "my-study")
list.files("my-study", recursive = TRUE, include.dirs = TRUE)
#>  [1] "config"                                  
#>  [2] "config/config_pass.json"                 
#>  [3] "config/ehr_config.json"                  
#>  [4] "data"                                    
#>  [5] "data/cohorts_data"                       
#>  [6] "data/cohorts_data/mimic_iv_demo_parquet" 
#>  [7] "data/source_data"                        
#>  [8] "data/source_data/mimic_iv_demo"          
#>  [9] "sql"                                     
#> [10] "sql/generated"                           
#> [11] "sql/generated/mimic_iv_demo"             
#> [12] "sql/generated/mimic_iv_demo/dur"         
#> [13] "sql/generated/mimic_iv_demo/ts"          
#> [14] "sql/mimic_iv_demo"                       
#> [15] "sql/mimic_iv_demo/concepts_sqls"         
#> [16] "sql/mimic_iv_demo/concepts_sqls/external"
#> [17] "sql/mimic_iv_demo/concepts_sqls/user"
Path Holds
config/ehr_config.json Project settings: database, source, paths, cohort profile
config/config_pass.json PostgreSQL and PhysioNet credentials
data/source_data/<source>/ Raw files from PhysioNet (unless raw_data_root points elsewhere)
data/cohorts_data/<source>_parquet/ The cohort, imported to Parquet
data/duckdb/ DuckDB files, when you use the DuckDB engine
sql/<source>/concepts_sqls/user/ Your own SQL concepts (see vignette("concepts"))
sql/generated/<source>/ SQL that rendehR generates from the concept dictionary

Keep config/config_pass.json and data/ out of version control: one holds a password, the other patient data.

The configuration file 

cat(readLines("my-study/config/ehr_config.json"), sep = "\n")
{
  "version": 1,
  "project": {
    "base_dir": "~/rendehr-docs/my-study"
  },
  "database": {
    "db_name": "rendehr",
    "credentials_path": "config/config_pass.json"
  },
  "source": {
    "src_name": "mimic_iv_demo"
  },
  "paths": {
    "raw_data_root": null,
    "cohort_parquet_root": "data/cohorts_data",
    "duckdb_root": "data/duckdb"
  },
  "concepts": {
    "ts_config_path": null,
    "dur_config_path": null,
    "user_concepts_path": null
  },
  "cohort": {
    "profile": "generic",
    "icd_filter_path": null,
    "icd_dict_path": null,
    "icd_proc_dict_path": null,
    "profiles": []
  }
}

The settings you are most likely to change:

  • database.db_name: the PostgreSQL database for this project. It defaults to "rendehr"; give every study its own database. Functions that take db_name use this value when you leave it out.
  • paths.raw_data_root: where the raw files are. null means data/source_data inside the project. Point it at a shared folder to reuse one download in several projects (below).
  • cohort.profile: "generic" (the default) or "scid", the spinal cord injury reference implementation. The profile decides two defaults. For an SCI cohort selected by diagnosis, "scid" adds the injury classification to the cohort table; any other cohort is left alone. And under "scid" the pipeline computes the comorbidity indices and injury severity scores unless told not to, while under "generic" they run only when asked.
  • cohort.icd_filter_path: the ICD list used when a call names no cohort.

Relative paths are relative to project.base_dir, which ehr_init_project() writes as an absolute path.

Credentials

config_pass.json holds the PostgreSQL login, and a PhysioNet login for the credentialed datasets:

{
  "postgres": {"host": "localhost", "port": 5432, "user": "postgres", "password": "..."},
  "physionet": {"username": "...", "password": "..."}
}

Environment variables take precedence over the file: PGHOST, PGPORT, PGUSER, PGPASSWORD and PGSSLMODE for PostgreSQL, PHYSIONET_USER and PHYSIONET_PASS for PhysioNet. The demo datasets are open and need no PhysioNet login.

Using a project

ehr_use_config() makes a project active for the R session, and ehr_check_config() reports what the settings resolve to:

ehr_use_config("my-study/config/ehr_config.json")
check <- ehr_check_config(quiet = TRUE)
check$ok
#> [1] TRUE
check$paths$raw_dir
#> [1] "~/rendehr-docs/my-study/data/source_data/mimic_iv_demo"

Without an active project, rendehR looks for config/ehr_config.json in the working directory, so setwd() into the project works too. You can also pass base_dir and db_name to each call.

Raw data

download_source() fetches a PhysioNet release into raw_data_root. It checks each file against the release’s SHA-256 manifest, reuses files that already match, and resumes interrupted downloads.

download_source("mimic_iv_demo")       # open
download_source("mimic_iv")            # needs a credentialed PhysioNet account

The supported releases and their size on disk as downloaded:

Source Release Size
MIMIC-IV demo 2.2 16 MB
MIMIC-III demo 1.4 94 MB
eICU-CRD demo 2.0.1 53 MB
MIMIC-IV 3.1 10 GB
MIMIC-III 1.4 6.2 GB
eICU-CRD 2.0 5.2 GB

The cohort import can cache the raw CSV as Parquet next to the project (data/raw_parquet_cache/). That takes about as much space again, and makes repeated imports of a full source much faster.

Several studies, one download

A study is a project: its own cohort, database and settings. Point raw_data_root at the folder that already holds the files and nothing is downloaded twice. Here a second project reuses the demo downloaded in vignette("rendehR"):

ehr_init_project(
  src_name = "mimic_iv_demo", base_dir = "sci-study",
  raw_data_root = normalizePath("rendehr-demo/data/source_data")
)
ehr_check_config(config_path = "sci-study/config/ehr_config.json", quiet = TRUE)$paths$raw_dir
#> [1] "~/rendehr-docs/rendehr-demo/data/source_data/mimic_iv_demo"

Set a different db_name in each project’s configuration and the two studies never touch each other’s tables.
